stats.fact: Hyperia reached v0.15.23 within 4 months of first release (March–July 2026)
Hyperia exposes 63 MCP tools over streamable HTTP — the most comprehensive MCP toolset of any terminal emulator
Warp terminal has 62,867 GitHub stars and recently open-sourced under AGPL-3.0
Hyper (original) has 44,636 GitHub stars — Hyperia is forked from this project
Hyperia is built with a Rust sidecar architecture decoupled from Electron for speed and reliability
Hyperia supports MCP connections from Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and Google Antigravity
Hyperia includes a built-in Ghost agent with streaming chat, tool use, and persistent memory
Hyperia's Pane Pulse watchdog re-submits prompts independently of any agent's loop for reliability
Hyperia is BSD-2-Clause licensed — permissive open source
Hyperia supports Stream Deck Plus as a physical control surface for terminal management

angles: Hyperia is the first terminal emulator designed from the ground up as an MCP-native agent platform
Unlike Warp's cloud-dependent AI, Hyperia runs entirely on your hardware with a consent-first model
The Rust sidecar architecture makes Hyperia faster and more reliable than Electron-only terminals
Pane Pulse watchdog solves the 'stalled agent' problem — a unique reliability feature
Hyperia's Ghost agent and Ferricula memory create a persistent AI co-pilot that remembers across sessions
Open source (BSD-2-Clause) vs Warp's AGPL — more permissive for commercial use
Built by a solo developer (kordlessagain / DeepBlue Dynamics) — indie alternative to VC-backed terminals
Stream Deck Plus integration makes Hyperia unique for power users and streamers
